content.content:
1	# Design — precision-first `declared-ready` run-SUFFICIENCY gate
2	
3	Date: 2026-06-30
4	Designs the upgrade of `scripts/hooks/declared-ready-stop.sh` from run-*existence*
5	("did ANY run-like command appear") to run-*sufficiency* ("did the agent exercise
6	the path it changed"), **without raising mute pressure**.
7	
8	Grounded in `empirical-declared-ready.md` (same dir): FP ≈ 65% (13/20) on current
9	fires; all 7 true positives *self-disclosed* their gap; the lowest-FP strategy is
10	diff-coverage gating + a self-disclosure FP-shield, degrading to a softer signal
11	where coverage tooling is absent.
12	
13	Environment facts verified for this design (`darwin`, this machine):
14	- `diff-cover`, `coverage`, `knip` are **absent globally** → coverage cannot be the
15	  default path; it is an *opportunistic best-signal* stage used only when a report
16	  already exists in the worktree.
17	- The session edit-list (`/tmp/claude-edited-files-<sid8>`, by
18	  `track-edits-session.sh`) is **session-cumulative**, not per-turn — it tells us
19	  *files touched this session*, never *lines changed this turn*.
20	- Per-turn changed lines are recoverable only from the transcript tail's
21	  `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit` `tool_use` blocks.
22	- `rg -P` (PCRE) and `shasum` are present (the current gate already uses both).
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 0. The core reframe — run-existence vs run-sufficiency
27	
28	```
29	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
30	│  TODAY (run-EXISTENCE)         did ANY allow-listed cmd appear this turn?  │
31	│    npm run ts:build ........... ✓ "ran"   ← scope substitution, SILENT LEAK│
32	│    pytest unrelated/ .......... ✓ "ran"   ← scope substitution, SILENT LEAK│
33	│    bash -n script.sh .......... ✗ stripped (good)                          │
34	│    i-dream widget status ...... ✗ not in allow-list ← real run, FALSE FIRE │
35	│                                                                            │
36	│  PRECISION-FIRST (run-SUFFICIENCY)  did a run exercise the lines I edited? │
37	│    coverage∩diff > 0 .......... sufficient → silent                        │
38	│    coverage∩diff == 0 ......... ran, but not the change → BLOCK            │
39	│    no coverage tooling ........ degrade: name-matched run → SOFT note;      │
40	│                                          nothing ran → BLOCK (today's case) │
41	│    agent self-disclosed gap ... reward correct hedge → SOFT note, never BLK │
42	└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
43	```
44	
45	The empirical pivot: the FPs are **concentrated and self-announced**, so the
46	single highest-leverage change is not a smarter run-detector — it is to *stop
47	blocking the agent when the agent already told the user what it didn't verify.*
48	The 7 TPs and ~6 of the 13 FPs are separated by exactly one text feature:
49	**did the message scope its own gap.** That is the precision axis.
50	
51	---
52	
53	## 1. SIGNAL — the exact detection signal (stage-1 best strategy, made concrete)
54	
55	The gate stays a four-stage AND for *eligibility* (Gate0 source-edited + Det1
56	claim survive unchanged — they already kill 1,279 + handle the conversational
57	case). The upgrade is the **decision pipeline that runs after eligibility**, in
58	strict precedence order. The first stage that matches decides; later stages do
59	not run.
60	
61	### Stage A — SELF-DISCLOSURE SHIELD (pure text, runs first, highest precision)
62	
63	The load-bearing empirical finding: **a self-disclosed gap is the agent doing the
64	right thing.** Blocking a correct hedge is the exact behavior that earns a mute.
65	So if the claim message *itself* scopes what it did not verify, the gate must NOT
66	block — it downgrades to a soft `systemMessage` (or silence), reinforcing rather
67	than trapping.
68	
69	Match (case-insensitive PCRE, against `claim_text` only — the last assistant
70	message, same source the current Det1 uses):
71	
72	```bash
73	DISCLOSE_RE='\b(not (yet )?(verified|exercised|tested|run|deployed|exercised in)|'\
74	'have(n.?t| not) (verified|exercised|tested|run|deployed|clicked)|'\
75	'compile[- ]?(only|checked)|type[- ]?check(s|ed)? (only|but)|'\
76	'can.?t (click|run|test|exercise|verify|deploy)[^.]*\b(here|from here|in this)|'\
77	'(only )?bash -n|--collect-only|--no-?emit|'\
78	'awaiting (you|your)|did you (see|notice)|what did you see|'\
79	'(want|should|shall) I (run|drive|start|verify|deploy|test)|'\
80	'haven.?t (yet )?(run|exercised))\b'
81	# Trailing user-observation question (the FP-3 mid-test-await shape):
82	TRAIL_Q='\?\s*$'
83	```
84	
85	Decision: if `claim_text` matches `DISCLOSE_RE` **or** ends in a trailing
86	question (`TRAIL_Q` on the last non-empty line) → **DOWNGRADE to soft note**
87	("you scoped the gap yourself; if you can exercise the changed path, do — else
88	this is a correct hedge"). Never block.
89	
90	Why this is the precision win, not a fragile broad regex: it does not try to
91	recognize *all* the ways a run can be insufficient (impossible to enumerate —
92	see `generalize-before-enumerate`). It recognizes the one thing that *cleanly
93	separates TP from FP in the corpus* — whether the agent admitted the gap. The 7
94	TPs would still be eligible to block (they don't all disclose in a *block-able*
95	shape — re-checked below), and 4 of the 13 FPs (mid-await, blocker,
96	two hedged-disclosure) are removed at zero new infrastructure.
97	
98	> Calibration note on the TPs: the empirical TPs *describe* their gap in the
99	> same message ("verified ruff but NOT the runtime effect"). Under a naive reading
100	> the shield would suppress all of them and the gate would never fire. It does
101	> not, because the shield is precise about the *shape* of disclosure: an
102	> **un-disclosed over-claim** is "Done. Type-checks clean." with no scoping clause
103	> on the same line/sentence as the success word. The TPs that pair a success word
104	> with an explicit "NOT verified" are the *gray zone* — and the correct product
105	> behavior for the gray zone is **soft note, not block** (the agent already told
106	> the user; a hard block adds nothing but friction). The gate's job is to BLOCK
107	> the silent over-claim and REINFORCE the disclosed one. Both behaviors lower mute
108	> pressure. The number of *hard blocks* drops; the number of *correct* hard blocks
109	> (silent over-claims) stays — that is precision, not coverage loss.
110	
111	### Stage B — COMMENT/DOCS-ONLY SHIELD (per-turn diff shape, pure text)
112	
113	FP-2: "comment pass complete", "added a 3-line comment" — nothing executable
114	changed, so there is no path to exercise; blocking is pure noise.
115	
116	Recover the **per-turn** changed lines from the transcript tail (NOT the
117	session edit-list, which is cumulative). For each `Edit`/`MultiEdit` `tool_use`
118	in this turn, the `new_string` is what landed; for `Write`, the whole `content`.
119	Classify the change as comment-only when every added/changed line is blank or a
120	comment in the file's language:
121	
122	```bash
123	# Pull this turn's added text from Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool_use blocks.
124	added=$(printf '%s\n' "$tail_json" \
125	  | jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]?
126	            | select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Edit" or .name=="MultiEdit" or .name=="Write"))
127	            | (.input.new_string // .input.content // (.input.edits[]?.new_string) // empty)' 2>/dev/null)
128	
129	# Comment-only if every non-blank added line starts with a comment marker for
130	# the edited language(s). Union of markers keeps it language-agnostic & cheap.
131	#   //  #  /*  *  */  --  <!--  ;  "  '''  """
132	if [ -n "$added" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$added" \
133	   | rg -v '^\s*$' \
134	   | rg -qvP '^\s*(//|#|/\*|\*|\*/|--|<!--|;|"|'\'''\'''\''|""")' 2>/dev/null; then
135	  comment_only=1   # nothing that ISN'T a comment/blank → no behavior changed
136	fi
137	```
138	
139	Decision: `comment_only=1` → **silent** (exit 0). This is the same "audit the
140	file's character before applying a global rule" instinct, applied to the diff.
141	
142	> Conservatism guard: the per-turn diff is reconstructed from the tail and is
143	> approximate. False *negative* here (treating a real change as comment-only) is
144	> the bad direction — it would silence a true block. So the test is strict: a
145	> *single* non-comment non-blank added line flips `comment_only` off. The cost of
146	> the rare miss (a genuinely comment-only change still blocks) is one soft note,
147	> not a wrong silence.
148	
149	### Stage C — RUN-SUFFICIENCY via diff-coverage (the real upgrade, opportunistic)
150	
151	This is the production-proven TIA/diff-cover signal: intersect *the lines changed
152	this turn* with *a coverage report produced by what ran this turn*. A changed line
153	with zero diff-coverage was edited but never executed — `npm run ts:build` and
154	`pytest unrelated/` both produce coverage that excludes the changed file, so both
155	correctly read as **insufficient**.
156	
157	Because `diff-cover`/`coverage` are absent globally, this stage is **opportunistic,
158	not mandatory**: it engages only when a coverage artifact already exists in the
159	project root (the agent or its test run produced one). Detection — look in the
160	project root of the edited file(s):
161	
162	```bash
163	# Coverage artifacts, in preference order (line-level → file-level):
164	#   coverage.xml / cobertura.xml         (Python/Java cobertura)
165	#   coverage/lcov.info / lcov.info       (JS/TS)
166	#   .coverage                            (python coverage, needs `coverage xml` first)
167	proj=$(dirname "$first_edited_src")            # walk up to nearest repo root
168	cov=""
169	for c in coverage.xml cobertura.xml coverage/cobertura-coverage.xml \
170	         coverage/lcov.info lcov.info; do
171	  if [ -f "$proj/$c" ] && [ "$proj/$c" -nt "$EDITED" ]; then cov="$proj/$c"; break; fi
172	done
173	```
174	
175	The `-nt "$EDITED"` freshness check is load-bearing: a *stale* coverage report (older
176	than this session's edits) proves nothing about this turn's run — treat it as
177	absent. (This is the `cache-externally-mutated-state` instinct: don't trust a
178	coverage report you can't prove is current.)
179	
180	When `cov` exists and `diff-cover` is installed:
181	
182	```bash
183	# diff-cover reports the % of git-diff lines covered. We only care: >0 or ==0
184	# for the changed source files. Scope the diff to this session's edits.
185	covered=$(diff-cover "$cov" --compare-branch=HEAD --fail-under=1 \
186	            --src-roots "$proj" 2>/dev/null; echo "exit:$?")
187	```
188	
189	Decision:
190	- changed lines covered (`diff-cover` reports >0% on the edited files) → **silent**
191	  (sufficient — a run touched the change).
192	- changed lines present but 0% covered → **BLOCK** with the scope-substitution
193	  reason ("you ran something, but it did not execute the lines you changed").
194	
195	If `cov` exists but `diff-cover` is not installed, do NOT shell out a hand-rolled
196	XML parse (fragile, and `generalize-before-enumerate` warns against inventing the
197	parser). Fall through to Stage D and emit a one-line `systemMessage` pointer:
198	`for line-precise sufficiency: pipx install diff-cover`.
199	
200	### Stage D — DEGRADED FALLBACK (no coverage tooling — the common case here)
201	
202	This is what fires on ~every turn on this machine, so it must be the *softer*
203	failure direction, not the hard one:
204	
205	- Det2 run-existence matches a known run command (today's allow-list, **plus**
206	  the FP-1 fix — see below) → **soft `systemMessage`**, not block. Rationale:
207	  something genuinely ran and we *cannot prove* it was insufficient without
208	  coverage, so we surface a reminder rather than trap. This converts FP-1-class
209	  cases (real run, narrow allow-list) from false *blocks* to harmless notes.
210	- Det2 matches nothing at all (no run, no pass/fail signal) → **BLOCK** — this is
211	  the original, well-justified behavior (`bash -n`-only / compile-only /
212	  collect-only / nothing). The 7 corpus TPs all land here (ruff-only, `bash -n`
213	  clean, compile-to-/tmp, tsc-only).
214	
215	FP-1 fix *inside the fallback only* (not promoted to "sufficient"): widen the run
216	detector to recognize real project-CLI runs that produced observed output, so a
217	genuine run downgrades block→note instead of false-blocking:
218	
219	```bash
220	# A Bash cmd whose tool_result shows a non-trivial, non-error result line counts
221	# as a "ran" (soft) — covers i-dream/project CLIs the static allow-list misses.
222	# Pair the cmd with its result: if the result has structured output (not an
223	# error/usage/empty), treat as run-existence → soft, never silent-sufficient.
224	```
225	Note this only moves the case from block→soft note in the *no-coverage* world; it
226	never asserts sufficiency. That keeps the scope-substitution leak closed (the
227	whole point) while removing the false *block*.
228	
229	### Stage E — FRONTEND OVERRIDE (the most-recurring leak class)
230	
231	Unit tests structurally cannot see RSC/hydration (§3d of the research; TP-2;
232	2026-05-08 / 2026-05-29 events). So for a changed `*.tsx`/`*.jsx` in a Next/RSC
233	project where the *only* run was `tsc`/`vitest`/`jest` (no `next build` / no
234	dev-server page load) **and Stage A did not fire** → **BLOCK** with the
235	RSC-specific reason. This is a targeted block, not a broad "screenshot every
236	tsx": Stage B (comment-only) and Stage A (disclosed) already carve out the
237	benign tsx edits, so what remains is exactly the un-disclosed "tsc green on a
238	client-interaction component" over-claim.
239	
240	```bash
241	# Next/RSC project detection (cheap, project-root):
242	is_next=0
243	[ -f "$proj/next.config.js" ] || [ -f "$proj/next.config.mjs" ] || \
244	  rg -q '"next"' "$proj/package.json" 2>/dev/null && is_next=1
245	# changed a *.tsx/*.jsx AND only tsc/vitest/jest ran AND not disclosed → BLOCK
246	```
247	
248	---
249	
250	## 2. PLACEMENT — Stop, with one PostToolUse companion
251	
252	**Decision: Stop hook (unchanged placement), reusing the existing direct
253	settings.json Stop registration.**
254	
255	The act-time-vs-stop-time tradeoff, made explicit:
256	
257	```
258	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
259	│ PreToolUse  catches an ACTION before it happens.                          │
260	│   "done/works/fixed" is a CLAIM, not a tool call → there is no action to  │
261	│   intercept. PreToolUse never sees the claim. WRONG layer for this gate.  │
262	│                                                                           │
263	│ Stop        catches the COMPLETED turn — the only point where the         │
264	│   turn-final claim text + the full set of this-turn runs both exist.      │
265	│   Sufficiency is a property of "claim vs what-ran-this-turn", which is     │
266	│   only knowable once the turn is closing. RIGHT layer.                     │
267	│                                                                           │
268	│ PostToolUse companion (already exists: track-edits-session.sh) maintains  │
269	│   the per-file edit set. We ADD nothing here — the per-turn diff comes     │
270	│   from the transcript tail at Stop, so no new PostToolUse hook is needed.  │
271	│                                                                           │
272	│ UserPromptSubmit  fires on the NEXT prompt — too late; the claim already   │
273	│   shipped to the user and the turn ended. (That placement suits           │
274	│   api-recovery-nudge, which is about the resuming turn, not this one.)      │
275	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
276	```
277	
278	A claim is caught at Stop because the claim only exists once the turn is final;
279	an action would be caught at PreToolUse, but this gate's trigger is a *claim*, not
280	an action. Stop is the only placement where "did what ran cover what changed" is
281	answerable. No companion hook is added — the existing `track-edits-session.sh`
282	PostToolUse already supplies Gate0's input, and the per-turn diff is read from
283	the transcript at Stop.
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 3. RESPONSE — stakes-scaled (three tiers), chosen to minimize mute pressure
288	
289	**A false BLOCK is what gets a hook muted; a precise NUDGE almost never does.**
290	So the response is tiered by how *certain* the gate is that the agent over-claimed:
291	
292	| certainty of un-exercised over-claim | response | mechanism |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| **High** — nothing ran (only compile/lint/collect/`bash -n`), un-disclosed; OR diff-coverage==0; OR Stage-E frontend | **BLOCK** (`decision:block`) — turn stays open, reason fed to agent | the 7 corpus TPs land here |
295	| **Medium** — a real run happened but sufficiency unprovable (no coverage tooling), OR agent self-disclosed the gap, OR diff-cover-absent-but-report-present | **SOFT** (`systemMessage`) — visible, non-blocking | converts FP-1 & disclosed-TP from block→note |
296	| **Low/none** — comment-only diff, exercised (coverage>0 or pass/fail signal) | **SILENT** (exit 0) | FP-2, true sufficiency |
297	
298	Loop-safety is preserved verbatim from the current gate: block once per claim
299	signature (`shasum` of `claim_text` in `/tmp/claude-declared-ready-<sid8>`); a
300	repeat of the same claim downgrades block→soft note ("not re-blocking…"). This is
301	already correct in the existing script — keep it.
302	
303	Why stakes-scaled beats a uniform block: the empirical FPs are not "the gate
304	fired when it shouldn't exist" — they are "the gate *blocked* when a *note* was
305	the right intensity." Demoting the uncertain cases to `systemMessage` removes the
306	mute trigger (a block that traps) while preserving the *signal* (the agent still
307	sees the reminder). Only the high-certainty silent-over-claim keeps the hard
308	block.
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 4. FP MITIGATIONS — the exact carve-outs
313	
314	In precedence order (each removes a named empirical FP bucket):
315	
316	1. **Self-disclosure shield** (`DISCLOSE_RE` + trailing-`?`) → downgrades
317	   block→soft. Removes: mid-test-await (FP-3, n=2), blocker/model-unavailable
318	   (n=1), and reclassifies the disclosed TPs from block→reinforce. *The single
319	   biggest precision lever* — the FP and TP cohorts are separated by this one
320	   text feature.
321	2. **Comment/docs-only diff shield** (per-turn added lines all comment/blank) →
322	   silent. Removes: comment-only edit (FP-2, n=2). Strict (one non-comment line
323	   flips it off) so it never wrongly silences a real change.
324	3. **Run actually exercised — coverage>0** (Stage C) OR **a pass/fail signal in
325	   tool_results** (existing Det2(b)) OR **a results table with observed `✓` in the
326	   assistant's own text** (FP-4 fix: extend the pass/fail scan to the assistant
327	   text block, not only tool_result blocks) → silent. Removes: "actually
328	   exercised" (FP-1, n=5) and the smoke-test-in-text case (FP-4).
329	4. **Project-CLI run widening** (Stage D, soft only) → real `i-dream`/project-CLI
330	   runs with observed output downgrade block→note instead of false-blocking.
331	   Closes the rest of FP-1 without ever asserting sufficiency.
332	5. **Per-item-in-audit guard** — require SUCCESS+SUBJECT within the **same
333	   sentence** (split `claim_text` on `[.!?\n]`, test the regex per-sentence),
334	   not anywhere in a long report. Removes: "## 1. llm-mini — done" inside a
335	   6-section cleanup audit (n=2). Concretely:
336	   ```bash
337	   # fire Det1 only if SOME single sentence carries BOTH success+subject
338	   hit=0
339	   while IFS= read -r s; do
340	     printf '%s' "$s" | rg -qiP "$SUCCESS_RE" && \
341	     printf '%s' "$s" | rg -qiP "$SUBJECT_RE" && { hit=1; break; }
342	   done < <(printf '%s' "$claim_text" | rg -oP '[^.!?\n]+[.!?]?')
343	   ```
344	6. **Gate0 unchanged** — source/test file edited this session AND at least one
345	   real source extension. Pure-docs turns never reach the pipeline.
346	7. **Coverage freshness** (`-nt "$EDITED"`) — a stale coverage report is treated
347	   as absent, never as proof of sufficiency.
348	8. **Loop-safe demotion** — same claim signature twice → soft note, never a
349	   second block. A persistent FP self-limits to one block.
350	
351	Combined day-one effect (mitigations 1, 2, 5 are pure-text, zero new dep):
352	empirical FP drops from **~65% → ~30%** before any coverage tooling is installed.
353	Stage C (coverage) takes it lower wherever a report exists. Stage D's degradation
354	ensures the no-tooling common case fails *soft*, not hard.
355	
356	---
357	
358	## 5. MUTE_RISK — honest assessment
359	
360	**LOW.**
361	
362	Reasoning, grounded in the numbers:
363	
364	- The gate is already extremely low-volume: **~30 fires across 959 transcripts**
365	  (≈1 per 120 turns). Even at today's 65% FP that is ~20 false fires over the
366	  *entire* corpus history — well under the threshold where an agent reaches for
367	  the mute file.
368	- The redesign's *net effect is fewer hard blocks, not more*. The sufficiency
369	  upgrade does not widen the fire set — it re-routes the existing fires: the
370	  un-exercised over-claims keep their block, the self-disclosed and
371	  actually-exercised cases demote to soft/silent. Mute pressure is a function of
372	  *false blocks*, and false blocks drop from ~13/20 toward ~6/20 day one
373	  (text-only shields) and lower with coverage.
374	- The one place mute risk could *rise* is Stage E (frontend BLOCK on tsc-only
375	  tsx): a `.tsx` developer who legitimately can't run a browser at Stop time
376	  would get blocked. Mitigated three ways: (a) Stage A demotes it if they
377	  disclosed ("type-checks clean, can't click here"), (b) Stage B silences
378	  comment-only tsx, (c) the existing per-claim loop-safety means a persistent
379	  case blocks exactly once. The residual is the genuinely-undisclosed
380	  "Done. Types clean." on an interaction component — which is precisely the
381	  pattern the gate *should* catch (TP-2). So Stage E's blocks are high-precision
382	  by construction.
383	- Escape hatch unchanged and honest: `touch ~/.claude/.no-declared-ready-gate`
384	  remains, named in every block reason. The redesign's goal is that an agent
385	  *never needs to reach for it* — and the path to that is the soft-tier, not a
386	  weaker signal.
387	
388	Why not MEDIUM: a MEDIUM rating would be honest if the upgrade *added* fire
389	surface (e.g. mandatory coverage that fires on every uncovered turn). It does the
390	opposite — coverage is opportunistic, the default path is *softer* than today, and
391	the two pure-text shields strictly *remove* false blocks. The only fire-surface
392	addition is Stage E, which is itself shielded by Stages A/B and is the
393	highest-precision class in the corpus.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## 6. Implementation sketch (precedence pipeline, drop-in for the existing gate)
398	
399	Keep lines 1–68 of the current gate verbatim (Gate0 + Det1 eligibility), with the
400	**per-sentence** Det1 fix (mitigation 5). Replace the Det2→block tail (lines
401	70–125) with the precedence pipeline:
402	
403	```
404	# eligibility survived (source edited + per-sentence claim)
405	A) self_disclosed?     → systemMessage(reinforce), exit          [FP-3, FP-blocker, disclosed-TP]
406	B) comment_only_diff?  → exit 0 (silent)                         [FP-2]
407	C) coverage report fresh & diff-cover present?
408	     diff>0 covered    → exit 0 (silent)                         [true sufficiency]
409	     diff==0 covered   → BLOCK (scope-substitution reason)       [the core upgrade]
410	D) exercised signal? (tool_result pass/fail OR observed ✓ table) → exit 0   [FP-1, FP-4]
411	   real run cmd (incl. project-CLI w/ output)? → systemMessage   [FP-1 soft]
412	   nothing ran?                                → BLOCK (today's reason)  [the 7 TPs]
413	E) tsx/jsx in Next + only tsc/vitest/jest + !disclosed → BLOCK (RSC reason) [TP-2]
414	loop-safe: same claim sig twice → demote BLOCK→soft note (unchanged)
415	```
416	
417	Each BLOCK emits `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; each SOFT emits
418	`{"systemMessage":…}`; SILENT is `exit 0`. All three contracts already exist in
419	the current script — no new plumbing.
420	
421	### Test plan (exercise the change — this gate is itself code)
422	Build a fixtures dir of synthetic Stop payloads from the corpus's 20 classified
423	fires (7 TP, 13 FP), feed each to the new script via stdin, assert:
424	- all 7 TPs → BLOCK or (disclosed-TP) SOFT — never SILENT
425	- all 13 FPs → SOFT or SILENT — never BLOCK
426	- the loop-safe second-fire demotes
427	Run it (`bash declared-ready-stop.sh < fixture.json`) and read the decision line
428	for each — do not declare this design "implemented" off a `bash -n`
429	(the very pattern the gate exists to catch).
430	
431	---
432	
433	## 7. What this design deliberately does NOT do
434	
435	- It does **not** mandate coverage tooling — that would make the gate fire on
436	  every uncovered turn and re-create mute risk. Coverage is opportunistic.
437	- It does **not** widen the run allow-list to assert *sufficiency* from a wider
438	  set of command names — that feeds the disease (run-existence ≠ run-sufficiency).
439	  Widening only ever demotes block→soft, never silences.
440	- It does **not** spawn an LLM/agent-judge per Stop — too slow/costly for a
441	  ~30-fire guard, and it reintroduces "trust the words." Reserve agent-judge as a
442	  future manual fallback for changed files with no coverage and no clear run.
443	- It does **not** hand-roll an lcov/cobertura parser — uses `diff-cover` when
444	  present, degrades gracefully when not.

# Design — precision-first `declared-ready` run-SUFFICIENCY gate

Date: 2026-06-30
Designs the upgrade of `scripts/hooks/declared-ready-stop.sh` from run-*existence*
("did ANY run-like command appear") to run-*sufficiency* ("did the agent exercise
the path it changed"), **without raising mute pressure**.

Grounded in `empirical-declared-ready.md` (same dir): FP ≈ 65% (13/20) on current
fires; all 7 true positives *self-disclosed* their gap; the lowest-FP strategy is
diff-coverage gating + a self-disclosure FP-shield, degrading to a softer signal
where coverage tooling is absent.

Environment facts verified for this design (`darwin`, this machine):
- `diff-cover`, `coverage`, `knip` are **absent globally** → coverage cannot be the
  default path; it is an *opportunistic best-signal* stage used only when a report
  already exists in the worktree.
- The session edit-list (`/tmp/claude-edited-files-<sid8>`, by
  `track-edits-session.sh`) is **session-cumulative**, not per-turn — it tells us
  *files touched this session*, never *lines changed this turn*.
- Per-turn changed lines are recoverable only from the transcript tail's
  `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit` `tool_use` blocks.
- `rg -P` (PCRE) and `shasum` are present (the current gate already uses both).

---

## 0. The core reframe — run-existence vs run-sufficiency

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TODAY (run-EXISTENCE)         did ANY allow-listed cmd appear this turn?  │
│    npm run ts:build ........... ✓ "ran"   ← scope substitution, SILENT LEAK│
│    pytest unrelated/ .......... ✓ "ran"   ← scope substitution, SILENT LEAK│
│    bash -n script.sh .......... ✗ stripped (good)                          │
│    i-dream widget status ...... ✗ not in allow-list ← real run, FALSE FIRE │
│                                                                            │
│  PRECISION-FIRST (run-SUFFICIENCY)  did a run exercise the lines I edited? │
│    coverage∩diff > 0 .......... sufficient → silent                        │
│    coverage∩diff == 0 ......... ran, but not the change → BLOCK            │
│    no coverage tooling ........ degrade: name-matched run → SOFT note;      │
│                                          nothing ran → BLOCK (today's case) │
│    agent self-disclosed gap ... reward correct hedge → SOFT note, never BLK │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The empirical pivot: the FPs are **concentrated and self-announced**, so the
single highest-leverage change is not a smarter run-detector — it is to *stop
blocking the agent when the agent already told the user what it didn't verify.*
The 7 TPs and ~6 of the 13 FPs are separated by exactly one text feature:
**did the message scope its own gap.** That is the precision axis.

---

## 1. SIGNAL — the exact detection signal (stage-1 best strategy, made concrete)

The gate stays a four-stage AND for *eligibility* (Gate0 source-edited + Det1
claim survive unchanged — they already kill 1,279 + handle the conversational
case). The upgrade is the **decision pipeline that runs after eligibility**, in
strict precedence order. The first stage that matches decides; later stages do
not run.

### Stage A — SELF-DISCLOSURE SHIELD (pure text, runs first, highest precision)

The load-bearing empirical finding: **a self-disclosed gap is the agent doing the
right thing.** Blocking a correct hedge is the exact behavior that earns a mute.
So if the claim message *itself* scopes what it did not verify, the gate must NOT
block — it downgrades to a soft `systemMessage` (or silence), reinforcing rather
than trapping.

Match (case-insensitive PCRE, against `claim_text` only — the last assistant
message, same source the current Det1 uses):

```bash
DISCLOSE_RE='\b(not (yet )?(verified|exercised|tested|run|deployed|exercised in)|'\
'have(n.?t| not) (verified|exercised|tested|run|deployed|clicked)|'\
'compile[- ]?(only|checked)|type[- ]?check(s|ed)? (only|but)|'\
'can.?t (click|run|test|exercise|verify|deploy)[^.]*\b(here|from here|in this)|'\
'(only )?bash -n|--collect-only|--no-?emit|'\
'awaiting (you|your)|did you (see|notice)|what did you see|'\
'(want|should|shall) I (run|drive|start|verify|deploy|test)|'\
'haven.?t (yet )?(run|exercised))\b'
# Trailing user-observation question (the FP-3 mid-test-await shape):
TRAIL_Q='\?\s*$'
```

Decision: if `claim_text` matches `DISCLOSE_RE` **or** ends in a trailing
question (`TRAIL_Q` on the last non-empty line) → **DOWNGRADE to soft note**
("you scoped the gap yourself; if you can exercise the changed path, do — else
this is a correct hedge"). Never block.

Why this is the precision win, not a fragile broad regex: it does not try to
recognize *all* the ways a run can be insufficient (impossible to enumerate —
see `generalize-before-enumerate`). It recognizes the one thing that *cleanly
separates TP from FP in the corpus* — whether the agent admitted the gap. The 7
TPs would still be eligible to block (they don't all disclose in a *block-able*
shape — re-checked below), and 4 of the 13 FPs (mid-await, blocker,
two hedged-disclosure) are removed at zero new infrastructure.

> Calibration note on the TPs: the empirical TPs *describe* their gap in the
> same message ("verified ruff but NOT the runtime effect"). Under a naive reading
> the shield would suppress all of them and the gate would never fire. It does
> not, because the shield is precise about the *shape* of disclosure: an
> **un-disclosed over-claim** is "Done. Type-checks clean." with no scoping clause
> on the same line/sentence as the success word. The TPs that pair a success word
> with an explicit "NOT verified" are the *gray zone* — and the correct product
> behavior for the gray zone is **soft note, not block** (the agent already told
> the user; a hard block adds nothing but friction). The gate's job is to BLOCK
> the silent over-claim and REINFORCE the disclosed one. Both behaviors lower mute
> pressure. The number of *hard blocks* drops; the number of *correct* hard blocks
> (silent over-claims) stays — that is precision, not coverage loss.

### Stage B — COMMENT/DOCS-ONLY SHIELD (per-turn diff shape, pure text)

FP-2: "comment pass complete", "added a 3-line comment" — nothing executable
changed, so there is no path to exercise; blocking is pure noise.

Recover the **per-turn** changed lines from the transcript tail (NOT the
session edit-list, which is cumulative). For each `Edit`/`MultiEdit` `tool_use`
in this turn, the `new_string` is what landed; for `Write`, the whole `content`.
Classify the change as comment-only when every added/changed line is blank or a
comment in the file's language:

```bash
# Pull this turn's added text from Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool_use blocks.
added=$(printf '%s\n' "$tail_json" \
  | jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]?
            | select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Edit" or .name=="MultiEdit" or .name=="Write"))
            | (.input.new_string // .input.content // (.input.edits[]?.new_string) // empty)' 2>/dev/null)

# Comment-only if every non-blank added line starts with a comment marker for
# the edited language(s). Union of markers keeps it language-agnostic & cheap.
#   //  #  /*  *  */  --  <!--  ;  "  '''  """
if [ -n "$added" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$added" \
   | rg -v '^\s*$' \
   | rg -qvP '^\s*(//|#|/\*|\*|\*/|--|<!--|;|"|'\'''\'''\''|""")' 2>/dev/null; then
  comment_only=1   # nothing that ISN'T a comment/blank → no behavior changed
fi
```

Decision: `comment_only=1` → **silent** (exit 0). This is the same "audit the
file's character before applying a global rule" instinct, applied to the diff.

> Conservatism guard: the per-turn diff is reconstructed from the tail and is
> approximate. False *negative* here (treating a real change as comment-only) is
> the bad direction — it would silence a true block. So the test is strict: a
> *single* non-comment non-blank added line flips `comment_only` off. The cost of
> the rare miss (a genuinely comment-only change still blocks) is one soft note,
> not a wrong silence.

### Stage C — RUN-SUFFICIENCY via diff-coverage (the real upgrade, opportunistic)

This is the production-proven TIA/diff-cover signal: intersect *the lines changed
this turn* with *a coverage report produced by what ran this turn*. A changed line
with zero diff-coverage was edited but never executed — `npm run ts:build` and
`pytest unrelated/` both produce coverage that excludes the changed file, so both
correctly read as **insufficient**.

Because `diff-cover`/`coverage` are absent globally, this stage is **opportunistic,
not mandatory**: it engages only when a coverage artifact already exists in the
project root (the agent or its test run produced one). Detection — look in the
project root of the edited file(s):

```bash
# Coverage artifacts, in preference order (line-level → file-level):
#   coverage.xml / cobertura.xml         (Python/Java cobertura)
#   coverage/lcov.info / lcov.info       (JS/TS)
#   .coverage                            (python coverage, needs `coverage xml` first)
proj=$(dirname "$first_edited_src")            # walk up to nearest repo root
cov=""
for c in coverage.xml cobertura.xml coverage/cobertura-coverage.xml \
         coverage/lcov.info lcov.info; do
  if [ -f "$proj/$c" ] && [ "$proj/$c" -nt "$EDITED" ]; then cov="$proj/$c"; break; fi
done
```

The `-nt "$EDITED"` freshness check is load-bearing: a *stale* coverage report (older
than this session's edits) proves nothing about this turn's run — treat it as
absent. (This is the `cache-externally-mutated-state` instinct: don't trust a
coverage report you can't prove is current.)

When `cov` exists and `diff-cover` is installed:

```bash
# diff-cover reports the % of git-diff lines covered. We only care: >0 or ==0
# for the changed source files. Scope the diff to this session's edits.
covered=$(diff-cover "$cov" --compare-branch=HEAD --fail-under=1 \
            --src-roots "$proj" 2>/dev/null; echo "exit:$?")
```

Decision:
- changed lines covered (`diff-cover` reports >0% on the edited files) → **silent**
  (sufficient — a run touched the change).
- changed lines present but 0% covered → **BLOCK** with the scope-substitution
  reason ("you ran something, but it did not execute the lines you changed").

If `cov` exists but `diff-cover` is not installed, do NOT shell out a hand-rolled
XML parse (fragile, and `generalize-before-enumerate` warns against inventing the
parser). Fall through to Stage D and emit a one-line `systemMessage` pointer:
`for line-precise sufficiency: pipx install diff-cover`.

### Stage D — DEGRADED FALLBACK (no coverage tooling — the common case here)

This is what fires on ~every turn on this machine, so it must be the *softer*
failure direction, not the hard one:

- Det2 run-existence matches a known run command (today's allow-list, **plus**
  the FP-1 fix — see below) → **soft `systemMessage`**, not block. Rationale:
  something genuinely ran and we *cannot prove* it was insufficient without
  coverage, so we surface a reminder rather than trap. This converts FP-1-class
  cases (real run, narrow allow-list) from false *blocks* to harmless notes.
- Det2 matches nothing at all (no run, no pass/fail signal) → **BLOCK** — this is
  the original, well-justified behavior (`bash -n`-only / compile-only /
  collect-only / nothing). The 7 corpus TPs all land here (ruff-only, `bash -n`
  clean, compile-to-/tmp, tsc-only).

FP-1 fix *inside the fallback only* (not promoted to "sufficient"): widen the run
detector to recognize real project-CLI runs that produced observed output, so a
genuine run downgrades block→note instead of false-blocking:

```bash
# A Bash cmd whose tool_result shows a non-trivial, non-error result line counts
# as a "ran" (soft) — covers i-dream/project CLIs the static allow-list misses.
# Pair the cmd with its result: if the result has structured output (not an
# error/usage/empty), treat as run-existence → soft, never silent-sufficient.
```
Note this only moves the case from block→soft note in the *no-coverage* world; it
never asserts sufficiency. That keeps the scope-substitution leak closed (the
whole point) while removing the false *block*.

### Stage E — FRONTEND OVERRIDE (the most-recurring leak class)

Unit tests structurally cannot see RSC/hydration (§3d of the research; TP-2;
2026-05-08 / 2026-05-29 events). So for a changed `*.tsx`/`*.jsx` in a Next/RSC
project where the *only* run was `tsc`/`vitest`/`jest` (no `next build` / no
dev-server page load) **and Stage A did not fire** → **BLOCK** with the
RSC-specific reason. This is a targeted block, not a broad "screenshot every
tsx": Stage B (comment-only) and Stage A (disclosed) already carve out the
benign tsx edits, so what remains is exactly the un-disclosed "tsc green on a
client-interaction component" over-claim.

```bash
# Next/RSC project detection (cheap, project-root):
is_next=0
[ -f "$proj/next.config.js" ] || [ -f "$proj/next.config.mjs" ] || \
  rg -q '"next"' "$proj/package.json" 2>/dev/null && is_next=1
# changed a *.tsx/*.jsx AND only tsc/vitest/jest ran AND not disclosed → BLOCK
```

---

## 2. PLACEMENT — Stop, with one PostToolUse companion

**Decision: Stop hook (unchanged placement), reusing the existing direct
settings.json Stop registration.**

The act-time-vs-stop-time tradeoff, made explicit:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PreToolUse  catches an ACTION before it happens.                          │
│   "done/works/fixed" is a CLAIM, not a tool call → there is no action to  │
│   intercept. PreToolUse never sees the claim. WRONG layer for this gate.  │
│                                                                           │
│ Stop        catches the COMPLETED turn — the only point where the         │
│   turn-final claim text + the full set of this-turn runs both exist.      │
│   Sufficiency is a property of "claim vs what-ran-this-turn", which is     │
│   only knowable once the turn is closing. RIGHT layer.                     │
│                                                                           │
│ PostToolUse companion (already exists: track-edits-session.sh) maintains  │
│   the per-file edit set. We ADD nothing here — the per-turn diff comes     │
│   from the transcript tail at Stop, so no new PostToolUse hook is needed.  │
│                                                                           │
│ UserPromptSubmit  fires on the NEXT prompt — too late; the claim already   │
│   shipped to the user and the turn ended. (That placement suits           │
│   api-recovery-nudge, which is about the resuming turn, not this one.)      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

A claim is caught at Stop because the claim only exists once the turn is final;
an action would be caught at PreToolUse, but this gate's trigger is a *claim*, not
an action. Stop is the only placement where "did what ran cover what changed" is
answerable. No companion hook is added — the existing `track-edits-session.sh`
PostToolUse already supplies Gate0's input, and the per-turn diff is read from
the transcript at Stop.

---

## 3. RESPONSE — stakes-scaled (three tiers), chosen to minimize mute pressure

**A false BLOCK is what gets a hook muted; a precise NUDGE almost never does.**
So the response is tiered by how *certain* the gate is that the agent over-claimed:

| certainty of un-exercised over-claim | response | mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **High** — nothing ran (only compile/lint/collect/`bash -n`), un-disclosed; OR diff-coverage==0; OR Stage-E frontend | **BLOCK** (`decision:block`) — turn stays open, reason fed to agent | the 7 corpus TPs land here |
| **Medium** — a real run happened but sufficiency unprovable (no coverage tooling), OR agent self-disclosed the gap, OR diff-cover-absent-but-report-present | **SOFT** (`systemMessage`) — visible, non-blocking | converts FP-1 & disclosed-TP from block→note |
| **Low/none** — comment-only diff, exercised (coverage>0 or pass/fail signal) | **SILENT** (exit 0) | FP-2, true sufficiency |

Loop-safety is preserved verbatim from the current gate: block once per claim
signature (`shasum` of `claim_text` in `/tmp/claude-declared-ready-<sid8>`); a
repeat of the same claim downgrades block→soft note ("not re-blocking…"). This is
already correct in the existing script — keep it.

Why stakes-scaled beats a uniform block: the empirical FPs are not "the gate
fired when it shouldn't exist" — they are "the gate *blocked* when a *note* was
the right intensity." Demoting the uncertain cases to `systemMessage` removes the
mute trigger (a block that traps) while preserving the *signal* (the agent still
sees the reminder). Only the high-certainty silent-over-claim keeps the hard
block.

---

## 4. FP MITIGATIONS — the exact carve-outs

In precedence order (each removes a named empirical FP bucket):

1. **Self-disclosure shield** (`DISCLOSE_RE` + trailing-`?`) → downgrades
   block→soft. Removes: mid-test-await (FP-3, n=2), blocker/model-unavailable
   (n=1), and reclassifies the disclosed TPs from block→reinforce. *The single
   biggest precision lever* — the FP and TP cohorts are separated by this one
   text feature.
2. **Comment/docs-only diff shield** (per-turn added lines all comment/blank) →
   silent. Removes: comment-only edit (FP-2, n=2). Strict (one non-comment line
   flips it off) so it never wrongly silences a real change.
3. **Run actually exercised — coverage>0** (Stage C) OR **a pass/fail signal in
   tool_results** (existing Det2(b)) OR **a results table with observed `✓` in the
   assistant's own text** (FP-4 fix: extend the pass/fail scan to the assistant
   text block, not only tool_result blocks) → silent. Removes: "actually
   exercised" (FP-1, n=5) and the smoke-test-in-text case (FP-4).
4. **Project-CLI run widening** (Stage D, soft only) → real `i-dream`/project-CLI
   runs with observed output downgrade block→note instead of false-blocking.
   Closes the rest of FP-1 without ever asserting sufficiency.
5. **Per-item-in-audit guard** — require SUCCESS+SUBJECT within the **same
   sentence** (split `claim_text` on `[.!?\n]`, test the regex per-sentence),
   not anywhere in a long report. Removes: "## 1. llm-mini — done" inside a
   6-section cleanup audit (n=2). Concretely:
   ```bash
   # fire Det1 only if SOME single sentence carries BOTH success+subject
   hit=0
   while IFS= read -r s; do
     printf '%s' "$s" | rg -qiP "$SUCCESS_RE" && \
     printf '%s' "$s" | rg -qiP "$SUBJECT_RE" && { hit=1; break; }
   done < <(printf '%s' "$claim_text" | rg -oP '[^.!?\n]+[.!?]?')
   ```
6. **Gate0 unchanged** — source/test file edited this session AND at least one
   real source extension. Pure-docs turns never reach the pipeline.
7. **Coverage freshness** (`-nt "$EDITED"`) — a stale coverage report is treated
   as absent, never as proof of sufficiency.
8. **Loop-safe demotion** — same claim signature twice → soft note, never a
   second block. A persistent FP self-limits to one block.

Combined day-one effect (mitigations 1, 2, 5 are pure-text, zero new dep):
empirical FP drops from **~65% → ~30%** before any coverage tooling is installed.
Stage C (coverage) takes it lower wherever a report exists. Stage D's degradation
ensures the no-tooling common case fails *soft*, not hard.

---

## 5. MUTE_RISK — honest assessment

**LOW.**

Reasoning, grounded in the numbers:

- The gate is already extremely low-volume: **~30 fires across 959 transcripts**
  (≈1 per 120 turns). Even at today's 65% FP that is ~20 false fires over the
  *entire* corpus history — well under the threshold where an agent reaches for
  the mute file.
- The redesign's *net effect is fewer hard blocks, not more*. The sufficiency
  upgrade does not widen the fire set — it re-routes the existing fires: the
  un-exercised over-claims keep their block, the self-disclosed and
  actually-exercised cases demote to soft/silent. Mute pressure is a function of
  *false blocks*, and false blocks drop from ~13/20 toward ~6/20 day one
  (text-only shields) and lower with coverage.
- The one place mute risk could *rise* is Stage E (frontend BLOCK on tsc-only
  tsx): a `.tsx` developer who legitimately can't run a browser at Stop time
  would get blocked. Mitigated three ways: (a) Stage A demotes it if they
  disclosed ("type-checks clean, can't click here"), (b) Stage B silences
  comment-only tsx, (c) the existing per-claim loop-safety means a persistent
  case blocks exactly once. The residual is the genuinely-undisclosed
  "Done. Types clean." on an interaction component — which is precisely the
  pattern the gate *should* catch (TP-2). So Stage E's blocks are high-precision
  by construction.
- Escape hatch unchanged and honest: `touch ~/.claude/.no-declared-ready-gate`
  remains, named in every block reason. The redesign's goal is that an agent
  *never needs to reach for it* — and the path to that is the soft-tier, not a
  weaker signal.

Why not MEDIUM: a MEDIUM rating would be honest if the upgrade *added* fire
surface (e.g. mandatory coverage that fires on every uncovered turn). It does the
opposite — coverage is opportunistic, the default path is *softer* than today, and
the two pure-text shields strictly *remove* false blocks. The only fire-surface
addition is Stage E, which is itself shielded by Stages A/B and is the
highest-precision class in the corpus.

---

## 6. Implementation sketch (precedence pipeline, drop-in for the existing gate)

Keep lines 1–68 of the current gate verbatim (Gate0 + Det1 eligibility), with the
**per-sentence** Det1 fix (mitigation 5). Replace the Det2→block tail (lines
70–125) with the precedence pipeline:

```
# eligibility survived (source edited + per-sentence claim)
A) self_disclosed?     → systemMessage(reinforce), exit          [FP-3, FP-blocker, disclosed-TP]
B) comment_only_diff?  → exit 0 (silent)                         [FP-2]
C) coverage report fresh & diff-cover present?
     diff>0 covered    → exit 0 (silent)                         [true sufficiency]
     diff==0 covered   → BLOCK (scope-substitution reason)       [the core upgrade]
D) exercised signal? (tool_result pass/fail OR observed ✓ table) → exit 0   [FP-1, FP-4]
   real run cmd (incl. project-CLI w/ output)? → systemMessage   [FP-1 soft]
   nothing ran?                                → BLOCK (today's reason)  [the 7 TPs]
E) tsx/jsx in Next + only tsc/vitest/jest + !disclosed → BLOCK (RSC reason) [TP-2]
loop-safe: same claim sig twice → demote BLOCK→soft note (unchanged)
```

Each BLOCK emits `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; each SOFT emits
`{"systemMessage":…}`; SILENT is `exit 0`. All three contracts already exist in
the current script — no new plumbing.

### Test plan (exercise the change — this gate is itself code)
Build a fixtures dir of synthetic Stop payloads from the corpus's 20 classified
fires (7 TP, 13 FP), feed each to the new script via stdin, assert:
- all 7 TPs → BLOCK or (disclosed-TP) SOFT — never SILENT
- all 13 FPs → SOFT or SILENT — never BLOCK
- the loop-safe second-fire demotes
Run it (`bash declared-ready-stop.sh < fixture.json`) and read the decision line
for each — do not declare this design "implemented" off a `bash -n`
(the very pattern the gate exists to catch).

---

## 7. What this design deliberately does NOT do

- It does **not** mandate coverage tooling — that would make the gate fire on
  every uncovered turn and re-create mute risk. Coverage is opportunistic.
- It does **not** widen the run allow-list to assert *sufficiency* from a wider
  set of command names — that feeds the disease (run-existence ≠ run-sufficiency).
  Widening only ever demotes block→soft, never silences.
- It does **not** spawn an LLM/agent-judge per Stop — too slow/costly for a
  ~30-fire guard, and it reintroduces "trust the words." Reserve agent-judge as a
  future manual fallback for changed files with no coverage and no clear run.
- It does **not** hand-roll an lcov/cobertura parser — uses `diff-cover` when
  present, degrades gracefully when not.

# Design — speculative-abstractions PRECISION-FIRST gate (anti-mute)

Hook id: `guard-speculative-export`
Status: design, not yet wired
Grounds: `empirical-speculative-abstractions.md` (same dir) — every number and
strategy below traces to that replay, not to invention.

The one-line thesis from the empirical work: **the only survivable mechanical
shape is V2 (zero-caller including the symbol's own def-file), fired post-write,
warn-only, diff-scoped to the symbol the tool call just added.** Anything broader
(V1/V3 = zero *external* caller) is ~85-88% FP and gets muted on day one;
anything blocking false-blocks the rename/wire-later churn that is inherent to
firing at write-time. This design is V2 + three hard gates + non-blocking nudge.

---

## SIGNAL — the exact detection signal that maximizes precision

Stage-1 best strategy from §4 of the empirical doc, made concrete:

> Fire only when a Write/Edit **adds a new `export function|const|type|interface|
> class|enum NAME`** to a TS/JS file, AND that `NAME` has **zero references
> anywhere in the project tree — including inside its own def-file** (V2 /
> `ignoreExportsUsedInFile` semantics).

Why this exact shape, not a broad regex:

- The naive "added an export" detector fires ~151× over the corpus at **~94% FP**
  (most exports are used). Unusable.
- The intuitive "zero *external* caller" (V1) fires 72× at **~85% FP**, because
  exported types used only inside their own file (`LlmStatus`, `ToolbarControl<T>`,
  `JobDisplayState`, the whole `claude-ipc` public-type surface) are a ubiquitous,
  correct TS pattern. A grep that excludes the def-file flags every one. This is
  the 58-symbol FP wall and the reason V1 is non-viable.
- **V2 — zero refs *including* own-file — fires 14× over the entire corpus, ~9
  true speculative-dead.** It is the only variant under ~35% FP, and it coincides
  exactly with two independent industry controls (ts-prune's `(used in module)`
  filter, knip's `ignoreExportsUsedInFile`). That external corroboration is the
  strongest evidence that "ignore exports used in their own file" is THE precision
  lever for this class.
- The diff is **free**: the tool call hands you the exact symbol added, so you
  never scan the backlog. That structurally excludes the whole-tree noise (the
  ~40-symbol `claude-ipc` library API) without any baseline file — you only ever
  evaluate *this* symbol.

The detection, concretely (reusing the proven `guard-duplicate-symbol.sh`
machinery — same project-root walk, same export-extraction regex family, same
build-artifact suppression):

```bash

#    kinds (functions AND types/interfaces/classes/enums AND non-fn const),
#    because the recorded S3s include both `deriveJobOutputStats` (fn) and
#    `JobOutputStats`/`TERMINAL_STATUSES` (type/const). Exclude `export {…}`
#    re-exports and `export default` (no stable name; barrel surface).
payload=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '
  .tool_input.content // .tool_input.new_string
  // ((.tool_input.edits // []) | map(.new_string // "") | join("\n")) // empty')

decl='export\s+(?:declare\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:abstract\s+)?'\
'(?:function|const|let|var|type|interface|class|enum)\s+'\
'([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)'

#    tree (incl. its own def-file), minus build artifacts, minus the bare
#    declaration line itself. If even one consuming reference exists → SUPPRESS.
#    `\b${name}\b` whole-word; count files, not lines.
refs=$(rg -n --no-heading "${globs[@]}" "\b${name}\b" "$root" 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vE "(^|:)[[:space:]]*export[[:space:]].*\b${name}\b[[:space:]]*[=:({<]?" )
# (the grep -v drops the declaration line so the symbol doesn't count as its own
#  caller; any remaining hit is a real use → suppress the fire)

     correctly, does not get muted.
  2. **Cheap to dismiss.** The residual ~35% FP (wire-later churn) costs one line
     to wave off; a dismissable advisory is not a mute trigger the way a false
     block is. Mute pressure scales with *interruption cost*, not FP rate.
  3. **Per-symbol-once + escape hatch.** It can't spam the same symbol, and a
     deliberate `// @public` / `// speculative-ok` marker stops it permanently for
     a reserved export — so the one population that *would* build resentment
     (intentional reserved API surface) has a one-token opt-out short of the global
     mute file.
- Global mute available and documented (`~/.claude/.no-speculative-export-gate`)
  but, by the volume + cost math above, an agent should almost never reach for it.

---

## Implementation notes

- **Reuse, don't reinvent.** ~80% of this hook already exists in
  `guard-duplicate-symbol.sh`: project-root walk (`package.json`/`.git`/
  `pyproject.toml`/`tsconfig.json` ancestor), the export-extraction regex family,
  `is_build_output()`, the generic-name stoplist, the `warn-log.sh` telemetry call,
  the `jq` payload extraction. Fork it; swap the "name exists elsewhere → block"
  body for "name has zero non-declaration refs → `additionalContext` nudge", add
  GATE 2's file-kind exemptions and GATE 3's test/citation/once-per-symbol logic.
- **Output contract:** `jq -nc --arg m "$msg" '{additionalContext:$m}'` (the
  channel that lands mid-session per `no-task-nudge.sh`), plus
  `bash ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/warn-log.sh --hook guard-speculative-export
  --heeded unknown` for fire-rate telemetry into `warn-events.jsonl` so the gate's
  own precision can be audited after deployment.
- **`async: true`** in settings.json — per-symbol `rg` over the tree must not
  block the turn.
- **Mute file:** `~/.claude/.no-speculative-export-gate` (first line of the script,
  `[ -f … ] && exit 0`).
- **Telemetry-driven tuning:** ship it warn-only, watch `warn-events.jsonl`
  fire-rate and (best-effort) heeded-rate for a few weeks. If real-world FP runs
  hotter than the replay's 35%, tighten GATE 2/3 before ever considering a block —
  and per the empirical doc's conclusion, probably never make it a block at all.

17	
18	## 0. The core design move (one sentence)
19	
20	Stop matching *authority words*; match the **conjunction** of (a) a claim shape
21	about how *existing* code/external-system works AND (b) the absence, in that same
22	turn's tool history, of any read of the thing being claimed about — then default
23	to a **nudge**, reserving a one-time block for the high-stakes + zero-evidence
24	corner only.
25	
26	This is the production "selection-before-flagging" principle (Claimify Selection /
27	CheckThat! verifiability filter, per the research in §3 of the empirical doc),
28	mechanized for a shell hook: the regex *narrows the candidate set*, and the
29	read-gate *enforces the actual signal* — "asserted without looking."

31	```
32	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
33	│  CURRENT  (vocabulary detector — ~2% precision)                            │

41	│        │                                                                   │

48	│         · authoring frame · person-owns homograph)                          │

50	│        ▼ no                                                                 │
