61	## 1. SIGNAL — the precise detection signal
62	
63	The signal is a **3-stage AND**, not a regex. Each stage discards a class the
64	empirical data proved to be noise. A fire requires all three.
65	
66	### Stage ① — claim-shape match (narrow the candidate set)
67	
68	Replace the single `AUTHORITY_RX` with **four small, named, anchored** alternations
69	— one per real failure shape in the 9-event corpus. Each is intentionally tight
70	(a verb/predicate *pattern*, not a noun list) so it admits only sentences that
71	make a checkable claim about *pre-existing* behavior.
72	
73	```bash
74	# ①a AUTHORITY — keep the genuinely-diagnostic present-tense authority predicates.
75	#     DROP the `owns the` / `mints the` branch entirely: 34/48 corpus fires (71%),
76	#     0 TP, pure homograph ("owns" = human/authoring far more than code-mechanism).
77	AUTHORITY_RX='\bis the (authority|source of truth|final (check|word|arbiter)|only (writer|owner|source)|hot path|canonical (source|owner)|single source of truth)\b|\bis the only (writer|owner|authority) (of|for|on)\b'
78	
79	# ①b CALL-CHAIN — "X <verb> (this|that|the) <path|endpoint|fn>" — the dominant real
80	#     shape (5/15 "Re-run button hits this path", 5/21 "daemon consumes ingest-queue").
81	#     Require a flow verb + a path/route/handler object so prose like "this helps the
82	#     user" can't match.
83	CALLCHAIN_RX='\b(hits|calls|consumes|invokes|reads from|writes to|routes? (to|through)|goes through|feeds into|is consumed by)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(this|that|the)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(path|route|endpoint|handler|queue|table|hook|consumer|reader|writer|callsite|function)\b'
84	
85	# ①c EXTERNAL-MECHANISM — "<ProperNounService> <renders|supports|returns|...>"
86	#     (5/21 "GitHub renders ansi in PR comments"). Anchored on a Capitalized service
87	#     token immediately before a behavior verb, so it can't fire on lowercase prose.
88	EXTMECH_RX='\b([A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]{2,}(\.[a-z]+)?)\s+(renders?|supports?|returns?|handles?|interprets?|strips?|escapes?|parses?|accepts?)\b'
89	
90	# ①d DEPENDENCY-MANIFEST — "<pkg> is (a|an) (direct )?(dep|dependency)" /
91	#     "is in package.json|Cargo.toml|go.mod|requirements.txt" (6/18 zod-transitive).
92	MANIFEST_RX='\bis (a |an )?(direct |transitive |dev )?(dependency|dep)\b|\bis (already |still )?(installed|in (package\.json|Cargo\.toml|go\.mod|requirements\.txt|pyproject\.toml|Gemfile))\b|\bnpm uninstall\b'
93	```
94	
95	**Why not also a scope-extrapolation regex** (the 6/25 "exoneration case is firm"
96	event)? Because "firm / holds / the case continues" carries *no* lexical claim
97	predicate — it is verifiable only against the *scope of the data the agent read*,
98	which a prose regex cannot reach without flooding FPs. That shape is explicitly
99	out of scope for this hook; it belongs to a different gate (a verdict-headline /
100	scope-creep check). Enumerating it here and *declining* it is the
101	`generalize-before-enumerate` discipline: I listed the 5 shapes, and this gate
102	owns 4 of them.
103	
104	A claim-shape match sets `shape=1` and records which class fired (used in the
105	nudge text and for the manifest subject-extraction in Stage ③).
106	
107	### Stage ② — evidence carve-out (the Claimify "Selection" analogue, expanded)
108	
109	This is where the existing hook is fatally thin: it carves out only on a `file:line`
110	or `[UNVERIFIED]`. The corpus proves the agent grounds claims *far more often* by
111	backtick-path, by a verification verb tied to a runtime read, or by writing in an
112	authoring frame. **Every one of the 48 FPs carried at least one of these.** Carve
113	out — stay silent — if the *same message* contains ANY of:
114	
115	```bash
116	# E1  file:line  OR  honest hedge tag  (the existing carve-out, kept verbatim)
117	CITE_RX='[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+:[0-9]+|\[UN(VERIFIED|CONFIRMED)\]'
118	
119	# E2  a backticked path — the agent cites by `path/to/file.ts` far more than by
120	#     :line (corpus records 33,35,44). A backtick span containing a / and a dot-ext.
121	BTPATH_RX='`[^`]*[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+[^`]*`'
122	
123	# E3  a verification verb bound to a runtime read — "confirmed", "verified",
124	#     "ran it", "tests pass", a PID, a launchctl/ps/curl read in the same breath
125	#     (records 02,11,18,20,25,33,35,39,45,46 — all FPs the current gate misses).
126	VERIFY_RX='\b(confirmed|verified|checked|i (ran|read|grepped|opened)|tests? (pass|passed)|launchctl|\bPID [0-9]+|exit[- ]status [0-9]|i (just )?(read|grepped|opened))\b'
127	
128	# E4  AUTHORING / PRESCRIPTION frame — the 17/48 design-doc shape. A markdown
129	#     ownership table row, an arrow-assignment, or future/modal "should/will own".
130	#     These are prescriptions about code the agent is DESIGNING, not assertions
131	#     about reality — non-verifiable by construction (CheckThat! verifiability).
132	AUTHORING_RX='\|[^|]*\b(owner|owns|authority|writer)\b[^|]*\||──?►|->[[:space:]]*hook|\b(should|will|would|propose[ds]?|let'\''s have|plan(ned)? to) (own|be the|act as)\b|state[- ]ownership map'
133	
134	# E5  PERSON / TEAM homograph — "whoever owns the schema", "the team that owns",
135	#     "owned by <name>". "owns" = human responsibility (corpus record 32).
136	PERSON_RX='\b(whoever|the (team|person|owner|dev|developer)|someone) (that |who )?owns\b|owned by [A-Z@]'
137	```
138	
139	If `shape=1` AND any of E1–E5 matches → **exit 0 (silent)**. Mechanically, this
140	single expansion takes the corpus from 48 fires to ~0-2 (per the empirical doc §4
141	projection: "every one of the 14 remaining carried a backtick-path, a verification
142	verb, a meta-quote, or an authoring frame").
143	
144	### Stage ③ — read-gate (the act-time selection signal, the precision lever)
145	
146	This is the new, highest-leverage check and the answer to the empirical doc's
147	deeper recommendation (§4): *"move the check to the act of asserting without a
148	preceding read."* A claim survives ① and ② only if it's a checkable assertion with
149	no in-message evidence. Stage ③ asks the one question that actually separates a TP
150	from an FP: **did the agent read the subject of the claim this turn?**
151	
152	```
153	For the claim's SUBJECT (the named file/module/dep/service), check whether THIS
154	TURN's tool history contains a Read/Grep/Glob whose target matches a subject token.
155	  · subject read this turn  → the agent looked; trust the claim → SILENT
156	  · subject NOT read         → asserted blind → candidate to fire
157	```
158	
159	**Subject extraction** (cheap, per claim class):
160	- *manifest*: the package token before "is a … dep" (e.g. `zod`). Subject read =
161	  a Read/Grep of `package.json` / `Cargo.toml` / `go.mod` / lockfile **this turn**,
162	  OR a Bash `cat`/`rg`/`jq` over a manifest file.
163	- *call-chain / authority*: the backticked or path-like noun in the sentence
164	  (`ingest-queue`, `rerun_tasks_for_job`, a route). Subject read = a Read/Grep/Glob
165	  whose `file_path`/`pattern`/`command` contains that token this turn.
166	- *external-mechanism*: the service is external (GitHub, fzf) — there is *no local
167	  file* to read, so the read-gate cannot clear it. For this class only, the carve
168	  that clears it is a web/lookup signal (E3's `confirmed`/`verified`, or a
169	  `WebSearch`/`WebFetch`/`curl` tool call this turn). If none → it fires (this is
170	  correct: 5/21 GitHub-ansi was asserted with neither a read nor a lookup).
171	
172	```bash
173	# Pull this turn's read/search targets (Read/Grep/Glob inputs + cat/rg/jq Bash).
174	read_targets=$(printf '%s\n' "$turn_json" \
175	  | jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]?
176	      | select(.type=="tool_use")
177	      | if   .name=="Read"  then (.input.file_path // empty)
178	        elif .name=="Grep"  then (.input.pattern // "") + " " + (.input.path // "")
179	        elif .name=="Glob"  then (.input.pattern // "")
180	        elif .name=="Bash" and ((.input.command//"")|test("\\b(cat|rg|grep|jq|head|less|fd|find)\\b"))
181	                            then (.input.command // "")
182	        else empty end' 2>/dev/null)
183	
184	# subject_token = the dominant noun extracted from the matched claim sentence.
185	# Fire only if the subject token does NOT appear in read_targets this turn.
186	if [ -n "$subject_token" ] && printf '%s' "$read_targets" | rg -qiF "$subject_token"; then
187	  exit 0   # read the subject this turn → silent
188	fi
189	```
190	
191	A fire is therefore: **a checkable claim about existing code/dep/external-system,
192	with no in-message evidence, in a turn that never read the named subject.** That
193	is the exact, non-fragile signal — the conjunction the corpus shows is empty of
194	false positives, because in all 48 FPs at least one of (evidence-in-message,
195	read-this-turn) was present.
196	
197	> **Why the read-gate is computed over the WHOLE turn, not the final message.**
198	> The claim lives in the last assistant text block (Stop-time, see §2). But the
199	> *read* that grounds it can be any tool call earlier in the same turn. So Stage ①
200	> reads the final block; Stage ③ walks the full turn's tool_use history. This is
201	> the act-time/stop-time split the analysis names, resolved by reading both.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 2. PLACEMENT — Stop hook, with a turn-history read-gate (not PreToolUse)
206	
207	**Decision: keep it a `Stop` hook** (current placement), but expand what it reads
208	from "final message only" to "final message + this turn's tool history."
209	
210	The analysis names the act-time-vs-stop-time tradeoff precisely: *"A Stop hook is
211	the right place to catch a **claim**, the wrong place to catch an **action** taken
212	on it."* For *this* pattern, the failure **is the claim** — the agent states how a
213	subsystem works in prose. There is no tool call to intercept; "asserting X is the
214	authority" is not a Bash/Edit a PreToolUse hook could see. The damage is the false
215	belief entering the record (a report, a proposal, the user's plan).
216	
217	| placement | what it can see | fit for *this* pattern |
218	|---|---|---|
219	| **PreToolUse** | a tool call's input, before it runs | **poor** — the claim is prose, not a tool call. PreToolUse never sees "X is the source of truth" because no tool carries it. (It is right for the *action-taken-on-a-claim* siblings — e.g. an Edit that broadens a filter on an unverified call-chain — but that's a different, action-shaped gate.) |
220	| **PostToolUse** | a tool's result, after it runs | poor — same reason; prose claims aren't tool results. |
221	| **Stop** | the completed turn: final prose **and** every tool_use/tool_result in it | **best** — the only place that sees the assertion in prose AND can check whether the subject was read this turn. The read-gate (Stage ③) is exactly the act-time signal, recovered *at* Stop by walking the turn's tool history. |
222	| UserPromptSubmit | next user prompt | irrelevant — too late, wrong actor. |
223	
224	So the right answer is not "move it to act-time"; it is **keep it at Stop and give
225	it act-time vision** by reading the turn's tool calls. Stop is also where the
226	agent can still act on the nudge before ending — a PreToolUse fire would interrupt
227	mid-thought with no claim to point at.
228	
229	The hook reads the **current turn** (from the last `user` message of type
230	non-tool-result back to the end) rather than the last 400 lines blindly, so the
231	read-gate is scoped to *this* turn's reads, not a stale read 5 turns ago. Concretely:
232	slice the tail at the last real user turn boundary.
233	
234	---
235	
236	## 3. RESPONSE — nudge by default, one-time stakes-scaled block only at the corner
237	
238	The current hook **blocks** in high-stakes repos. A block on a 98%-FP detector is
239	the direct cause of mute pressure: the first false block teaches the agent the
240	hook is wrong, and the cheapest fix is `touch ~/.claude/.no-structural-claim-gate`.
241	
242	The redesign makes the detector ~0 FP first (§1), which *earns back* the right to
243	some friction — but the response still defaults to the lowest-pressure form:
244	
245	| condition | response | rationale |
246	|---|---|---|
247	| shape ∧ no-evidence ∧ no-read, **low-stakes** | `systemMessage` **nudge** (non-blocking) | a precise nudge rarely gets muted; the agent reads it and self-corrects or proceeds. |
248	| shape ∧ no-evidence ∧ no-read, **high-stakes**, **first time this claim** | one-time `decision:block` with a DO-CONFIRM | only at the corner where a wrong structural claim actually ships cost (Versable, gcc). Even here it blocks **once per claim-signature** then steps aside to a note — a residual FP costs at most one extra turn, never a trap. |
249	| same claim-signature already actioned | `systemMessage` note, then silent | loop-safe; never re-blocks the same sentence. |
250	
251	The block reason is **specific to the matched class** — it names the subject and
252	says "you didn't read `<subject>` this turn," which is falsifiable and actionable,
253	unlike the current generic "you cite no file:line." A nudge the agent can verify
254	against ("I *did* read it — false positive") is a nudge it dismisses in one line
255	rather than mutes.
256	
257	**Why not block in low-stakes too:** the empirical lesson is unambiguous — false
258	*blocks* drive mutes, false *nudges* mostly don't. Defaulting to nudge keeps mute
259	pressure at the floor; the high-stakes one-time block is the only place the
260	expected cost of a missed structural claim (a shipped wrong belief in production
261	code) justifies the friction, and even there the step-aside caps the downside.
262	
263	---
264	
265	## 4. FP MITIGATIONS — the exact carve-outs
266	
267	Each is grounded in a specific corpus FP class (counts from the n=48 hand-read):
268	
269	| # | carve-out | clears | corpus class (count) |
270	|---|---|---|---|
271	| M1 | **Drop the `owns/mints the` branch** from the regex entirely | 34/48 fires | homograph noise (71% of all fires, 0 TP) |
272	| M2 | **`file:line` cite** (E1, kept) | grounded claims | existing carve, retained |
273	| M3 | **`[UNVERIFIED]`/`[UNCONFIRMED]` hedge tag** (E1, kept) | honestly-hedged | the agent flagged its own uncertainty |
274	| M4 | **backtick-path cite** `` `dir/file.ts` `` (E2) | path-grounded | records 33,35,44 — agent cites by path not :line |
275	| M5 | **verify-verb + runtime read** (E3): confirmed/verified/ran-it/tests-pass/PID/launchctl | empirically-grounded | records 02,11,18,20,25,33,35,39,45,46 (11/48) |
276	| M6 | **authoring/prescription frame** (E4): ownership table row, `──►` arrow, "should/will own", "state-ownership map" | design prescriptions | records 19,24,38,40,41,47 (17/48) |
277	| M7 | **person/team homograph** (E5): "whoever owns", "owned by <Name>" | human-responsibility "owns" | record 32 (6/48) |
278	| M8 | **read-this-turn of the subject** (Stage ③): Read/Grep/Glob/cat/rg of a file matching the subject token | the agent looked | the act-time signal; the single strongest separator |
279	| M9 | **external-mechanism web/lookup signal**: WebSearch/WebFetch/curl this turn, or E3 verify-verb | looked-up external behavior | record 11 (fzf version-checked) |
280	| M10 | **meta-discussion guard**: claim text contains a quoted-pattern marker (`structural-claim`, `AUTHORITY_RX`, "the atone pattern", "this gate/hook") | discussing the rule itself | records 08,13 (4/48) — the hook firing on a discussion of the hook |
281	| M11 | **docs-only turn**: if this turn edited only `.md`/`.txt` and made no code edit, demote any fire to silent unless high-stakes | design-doc prose | most authoring lives in docs; pairs with M6 |
282	| M12 | **loop-safe signature** (kept): one action per claim-hash, then step aside | re-fires on the same sentence | existing, retained |
283	
284	Carve-out evaluation order is **cheapest-first and OR-short-circuit**: E1→E2 (regex
285	on text, instant) → E4/E5/E10 (regex on text) → E3 (regex) → ③ read-gate (needs jq
286	over turn tool_use, most expensive). Any hit → silent.
287	
288	**Test corpus (regression):** the 9 real S3 events in
289	`events-structural-claim-without-reading-code.md` are the recall set; the 48
290	would-fire records in `empirical-structural-claim.md` are the precision set. The
291	redesign must (a) keep firing on the genuine blind-assertion shapes — 5/15
292	call-chain, 5/21 daemon-consumes, 5/21 GitHub-ansi, 6/18 zod-manifest, all of
293	which were asserted with no read and no evidence — and (b) drop all 48 corpus FPs.
294	Build a `replay-v2.py` that ports stages ①②③ and run it over the same 959
295	transcripts; ship only if precision-set fires ≤ 2 AND each of the 9 recall events
296	(replayed with its real turn's tool history) still fires.
297	
298	---
299	
300	## 5. MUTE_RISK — honest assessment: **LOW**
301	
302	| factor | current hook | redesign |
303	|---|---|---|
304	| corpus FP rate | ~98-100% (48/48) | projected ~0-2 fires total (selection gate) |
305	| default response | block (high-stakes) | nudge; block only at high-stakes ∧ blind corner |
306	| first-fire experience | almost certainly a false block → mute | almost certainly silent; if it fires, it names an unread subject (falsifiable) |
307	| dismissal cost on FP | mute the hook | one line ("I read it / verified out-of-band"), step-aside |
308	
309	**Low, with two honest caveats:**
310	
311	1. **Recall is structurally bounded** — the empirical doc is blunt that even a
312	   broadened *prose* regex reaches maybe ~4-5 of the 9 shapes; the scope-creep
313	   (6/25) and tooling-mangle (6/12) shapes are out of this gate's reach by
314	   construction (the latter is already owned by the `rg -r` replace-guard). This
315	   redesign optimizes **precision** (the mute driver) and accepts that it is a
316	   *partial* recall net. That is the correct trade: a low-recall, ~0-FP nudge is
317	   strictly better than a high-recall block that gets muted to zero recall on day
318	   one. A muted hook has 0% recall.
319	
320	2. **The read-gate has a real-but-narrow FP surface**: an agent that read the
321	   subject in a *prior* turn (then asserts this turn without re-reading) would fire.
322	   This is mitigated by scoping ③ to the current turn *and* by M5 (if the agent
323	   read it before, it almost always says "confirmed/I read" in the claim, clearing
324	   via E3). The residual case — read last turn, asserted bare this turn, no verify
325	   verb — fires a *nudge* the agent dismisses in one line. Acceptable: a nudge, not
326	   a block, and rare.
327	
328	The single thing that makes this mutable-resistant: **a fire is falsifiable.** The
329	agent can always answer "I read `<subject>`" or "I verified it" and the message
330	self-documents that the hook accepts that answer (it won't re-fire). The current
331	hook's generic "you cite no file:line" is not falsifiable in the same way (the
332	agent *did* cite, by path or by having read) — which is exactly why it reads as
333	broken and invites the mute.
334	
335	---
336	
337	## 6. Implementation sketch (drop-in for `guard-structural-claim.sh`)
338	
339	Reuses the proven idioms from `declared-ready-stop.sh` (turn-tail read, jq over
340	tool_use, loop-safe signature, stakes-tier.sh) so this is a contained edit, not a
341	new subsystem.
342	
343	```bash
344	#!/usr/bin/env bash
345	set -uo pipefail
346	[ -f "$HOME/.claude/.no-structural-claim-gate" ] && exit 0
347	input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
348	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
349	
350	sid=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.session_id // empty'); sid8="${sid:0:8}"
351	tp=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.transcript_path // empty')
352	[ -n "$sid" ] && [ -f "$tp" ] || exit 0
353	
354	# Scope to the CURRENT turn: tail, then cut at the last real (non-tool-result) user msg.
355	tail_json=$(tail -n 600 "$tp" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$tail_json" ] || exit 0
356	last_asst=$(printf '%s\n' "$tail_json" | jq -rc 'select(.type=="assistant")' | tail -n 1)
357	text=$(printf '%s' "$last_asst" | jq -r '.message.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text')
358	[ -n "$text" ] || exit 0
359	
360	# Stage ① — which claim class? (sets $shape, $klass; tightened regexes from §1)
361	shape=0; klass=""
362	for pair in "authority:$AUTHORITY_RX" "callchain:$CALLCHAIN_RX" \
363	            "extmech:$EXTMECH_RX" "manifest:$MANIFEST_RX"; do
364	  k=${pair%%:*}; rx=${pair#*:}
365	  if printf '%s' "$text" | rg -qiP "$rx" 2>/dev/null; then shape=1; klass="$k"; break; fi
366	done
367	[ "$shape" = 1 ] || exit 0
368	
369	# Stage ② — evidence carve-out (E1..E5 + M10 meta + M11 docs-only). OR short-circuit.
370	for rx in "$CITE_RX" "$BTPATH_RX" "$AUTHORING_RX" "$PERSON_RX" "$VERIFY_RX" "$META_RX"; do
371	  printf '%s' "$text" | rg -qiP "$rx" 2>/dev/null && exit 0
372	done
373	
374	# Stage ③ — read-gate: did THIS TURN read the claim subject?
375	subject=$(extract_subject "$text" "$klass")          # backtick noun / pkg token / path
376	read_targets=$(printf '%s\n' "$tail_json" | jq -r '...Read/Grep/Glob/cat/rg inputs...')
377	[ -n "$subject" ] && printf '%s' "$read_targets" | rg -qiF "$subject" && exit 0
378	# extmech: also clear on a WebSearch/WebFetch/curl this turn (M9)
379	[ "$klass" = extmech ] && printf '%s\n' "$tail_json" \
380	  | jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant")|.message.content[]?|select(.type=="tool_use")|.name' \
381	  | rg -qi 'WebSearch|WebFetch' && exit 0
382	
383	# ── Survived all three → fire. Loop-safe + stakes-scaled (§3). ────────────────
384	stakes=$(bash "$HOME/.claude/scripts/stakes-tier.sh" "$(printf '%s' "$input"|jq -r '.cwd//empty')")
385	MARK="/tmp/claude-structural-claim-${sid8}"
386	sig=$(printf '%s' "$text" | shasum | awk '{print $1}')
387	prev=$(cat "$MARK" 2>/dev/null || true)
388	note="⚠ structural-claim — your message states how '$subject' works ($klass) but this turn shows no Read/Grep of it and no in-message cite. Pattern-matching ≠ evidence. Read $subject or name its file:line. FP (you read it / verified out-of-band)? Say so. Mute: touch ~/.claude/.no-structural-claim-gate"
389	if [ "$sig" = "$prev" ]; then jq -cn --arg m "$note" '{systemMessage:$m}'; exit 0; fi
390	printf '%s' "$sig" > "$MARK"
391	if [ "$stakes" = high ]; then
392	  jq -cn --arg r "⛔ $note" '{decision:"block",reason:$r}'
393	else
394	  jq -cn --arg m "$note" '{systemMessage:$m}'
395	fi
396	exit 0
397	```
398	
399	(`extract_subject` and the four `*_RX` constants are the §1 definitions; `META_RX`
400	= `structural-claim|AUTHORITY_RX|atone pattern|this (gate|hook)`.)
401	
402	---
403	
404	## 7. What changed vs the current hook, in one table
405	
406	| dimension | current | redesign |
407	|---|---|---|
408	| detector | one broad authority-noun regex | 4 tight claim-shape regexes (authority/call-chain/ext-mech/manifest), `owns the` dropped |
409	| selection gate | none — fires on vocabulary | **read-gate**: fire only if the subject was NOT read this turn |
410	| carve-outs | `file:line` + `[UNVERIFIED]` only | + backtick-path, verify-verb+runtime, authoring-frame, person-homograph, meta, web-lookup, read-this-turn (M1–M12) |
411	| placement | Stop (final msg only) | Stop (final msg **+ this turn's tool history**) |
412	| response | high-stakes BLOCK first | nudge default; one-time block only at high-stakes ∧ blind corner |
413	| corpus FP | ~98-100% (48/48) | projected ~0-2 total |
414	| mute risk | **maximal** (block on noise) | **low** (silent ~always; fires are falsifiable nudges) |
415	| recall | ~1 of 9 shapes | ~4-5 of 9 (call-chain, manifest, ext-mech, authority added); scope-creep + tooling-mangle out of scope by design |

# Precision-first redesign — `guard-structural-claim` (the unmutable version)

**Date:** 2026-06-30 · **Author session:** s3-gate-leak workflow (task #19)
**Grounds:** `empirical-structural-claim.md` (FP replay, n=48 full-population),
`events-structural-claim-without-reading-code.md` (9 real S3 events), `analysis.md`
(cross-cutting "narrow detector vs broad failure" + "Stop-time vs act-time").
**Current code:** `scripts/hooks/guard-structural-claim.sh`.

The bar set by the task: an agent should ~never need to mute this. The current
hook earns a mute on its first fire — empirically **0/48 true positives, ~98-100%
FP**, and its high-stakes mode is a *block*. A block on noise is precisely what
gets a hook muted, and a muted hook enforces nothing. This redesign trades the
broad vocabulary regex for a **two-condition selection gate** that the empirical
data proves lands near 0 FP.

---

## 0. The core design move (one sentence)

Stop matching *authority words*; match the **conjunction** of (a) a claim shape
about how *existing* code/external-system works AND (b) the absence, in that same
turn's tool history, of any read of the thing being claimed about — then default
to a **nudge**, reserving a one-time block for the high-stakes + zero-evidence
corner only.

This is the production "selection-before-flagging" principle (Claimify Selection /
CheckThat! verifiability filter, per the research in §3 of the empirical doc),
mechanized for a shell hook: the regex *narrows the candidate set*, and the
read-gate *enforces the actual signal* — "asserted without looking."

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  CURRENT  (vocabulary detector — ~2% precision)                            │
│    last-msg matches AUTHORITY_RX ──► (no file:line) ──► BLOCK / note        │
│    └─ fires on "the modal owns the view hook" in a design doc you're        │
│       AUTHORING. No notion of read-history. 0/48 TP.                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  REDESIGN  (selection gate — claim-shape ∧ no-read-of-subject)             │
│                                                                            │
│    last assistant msg                                                      │
│        │                                                                   │
│        ▼                                                                   │
│   ① CLAIM-SHAPE?  (authority | call-chain | external-mech | manifest)      │
│        │ no → silent                                                        │
│        ▼ yes                                                                │
│   ② EVIDENCE CARVE-OUT in same msg?                                         │
│        (file:line · `backtick-path` · verify-verb+runtime · [UNVERIFIED]    │
│         · authoring frame · person-owns homograph)                          │
│        │ yes → silent  ◄── kills ~all 48 corpus FPs                         │
│        ▼ no                                                                 │
│   ③ READ-GATE: did THIS TURN Read/Grep/Glob a file whose name matches a     │
│        token of the claim's subject?                                        │
│        │ yes (read the subject) → silent  ◄── "you looked; trust it"        │
│        ▼ no (asserted blind)                                                │
│   ④ RESPOND: nudge (default) · stakes-scaled one-time block (high+blind)    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. SIGNAL — the precise detection signal

The signal is a **3-stage AND**, not a regex. Each stage discards a class the
empirical data proved to be noise. A fire requires all three.

### Stage ① — claim-shape match (narrow the candidate set)

Replace the single `AUTHORITY_RX` with **four small, named, anchored** alternations
— one per real failure shape in the 9-event corpus. Each is intentionally tight
(a verb/predicate *pattern*, not a noun list) so it admits only sentences that
make a checkable claim about *pre-existing* behavior.

```bash
# ①a AUTHORITY — keep the genuinely-diagnostic present-tense authority predicates.
#     DROP the `owns the` / `mints the` branch entirely: 34/48 corpus fires (71%),
#     0 TP, pure homograph ("owns" = human/authoring far more than code-mechanism).
AUTHORITY_RX='\bis the (authority|source of truth|final (check|word|arbiter)|only (writer|owner|source)|hot path|canonical (source|owner)|single source of truth)\b|\bis the only (writer|owner|authority) (of|for|on)\b'

# ①b CALL-CHAIN — "X <verb> (this|that|the) <path|endpoint|fn>" — the dominant real
#     shape (5/15 "Re-run button hits this path", 5/21 "daemon consumes ingest-queue").
#     Require a flow verb + a path/route/handler object so prose like "this helps the
#     user" can't match.
CALLCHAIN_RX='\b(hits|calls|consumes|invokes|reads from|writes to|routes? (to|through)|goes through|feeds into|is consumed by)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(this|that|the)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(path|route|endpoint|handler|queue|table|hook|consumer|reader|writer|callsite|function)\b'

# ①c EXTERNAL-MECHANISM — "<ProperNounService> <renders|supports|returns|...>"
#     (5/21 "GitHub renders ansi in PR comments"). Anchored on a Capitalized service
#     token immediately before a behavior verb, so it can't fire on lowercase prose.
EXTMECH_RX='\b([A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]{2,}(\.[a-z]+)?)\s+(renders?|supports?|returns?|handles?|interprets?|strips?|escapes?|parses?|accepts?)\b'

# ①d DEPENDENCY-MANIFEST — "<pkg> is (a|an) (direct )?(dep|dependency)" /
#     "is in package.json|Cargo.toml|go.mod|requirements.txt" (6/18 zod-transitive).
MANIFEST_RX='\bis (a |an )?(direct |transitive |dev )?(dependency|dep)\b|\bis (already |still )?(installed|in (package\.json|Cargo\.toml|go\.mod|requirements\.txt|pyproject\.toml|Gemfile))\b|\bnpm uninstall\b'
```

**Why not also a scope-extrapolation regex** (the 6/25 "exoneration case is firm"
event)? Because "firm / holds / the case continues" carries *no* lexical claim
predicate — it is verifiable only against the *scope of the data the agent read*,
which a prose regex cannot reach without flooding FPs. That shape is explicitly
out of scope for this hook; it belongs to a different gate (a verdict-headline /
scope-creep check). Enumerating it here and *declining* it is the
`generalize-before-enumerate` discipline: I listed the 5 shapes, and this gate
owns 4 of them.

A claim-shape match sets `shape=1` and records which class fired (used in the
nudge text and for the manifest subject-extraction in Stage ③).

### Stage ② — evidence carve-out (the Claimify "Selection" analogue, expanded)

This is where the existing hook is fatally thin: it carves out only on a `file:line`
or `[UNVERIFIED]`. The corpus proves the agent grounds claims *far more often* by
backtick-path, by a verification verb tied to a runtime read, or by writing in an
authoring frame. **Every one of the 48 FPs carried at least one of these.** Carve
out — stay silent — if the *same message* contains ANY of:

```bash
# E1  file:line  OR  honest hedge tag  (the existing carve-out, kept verbatim)
CITE_RX='[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+:[0-9]+|\[UN(VERIFIED|CONFIRMED)\]'

# E2  a backticked path — the agent cites by `path/to/file.ts` far more than by
#     :line (corpus records 33,35,44). A backtick span containing a / and a dot-ext.
BTPATH_RX='`[^`]*[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+[^`]*`'

# E3  a verification verb bound to a runtime read — "confirmed", "verified",
#     "ran it", "tests pass", a PID, a launchctl/ps/curl read in the same breath
#     (records 02,11,18,20,25,33,35,39,45,46 — all FPs the current gate misses).
VERIFY_RX='\b(confirmed|verified|checked|i (ran|read|grepped|opened)|tests? (pass|passed)|launchctl|\bPID [0-9]+|exit[- ]status [0-9]|i (just )?(read|grepped|opened))\b'

# E4  AUTHORING / PRESCRIPTION frame — the 17/48 design-doc shape. A markdown
#     ownership table row, an arrow-assignment, or future/modal "should/will own".
#     These are prescriptions about code the agent is DESIGNING, not assertions
#     about reality — non-verifiable by construction (CheckThat! verifiability).
AUTHORING_RX='\|[^|]*\b(owner|owns|authority|writer)\b[^|]*\||──?►|->[[:space:]]*hook|\b(should|will|would|propose[ds]?|let'\''s have|plan(ned)? to) (own|be the|act as)\b|state[- ]ownership map'

# E5  PERSON / TEAM homograph — "whoever owns the schema", "the team that owns",
#     "owned by <name>". "owns" = human responsibility (corpus record 32).
PERSON_RX='\b(whoever|the (team|person|owner|dev|developer)|someone) (that |who )?owns\b|owned by [A-Z@]'
```

If `shape=1` AND any of E1–E5 matches → **exit 0 (silent)**. Mechanically, this
single expansion takes the corpus from 48 fires to ~0-2 (per the empirical doc §4
projection: "every one of the 14 remaining carried a backtick-path, a verification
verb, a meta-quote, or an authoring frame").

### Stage ③ — read-gate (the act-time selection signal, the precision lever)

This is the new, highest-leverage check and the answer to the empirical doc's
deeper recommendation (§4): *"move the check to the act of asserting without a
preceding read."* A claim survives ① and ② only if it's a checkable assertion with
no in-message evidence. Stage ③ asks the one question that actually separates a TP
from an FP: **did the agent read the subject of the claim this turn?**

```
For the claim's SUBJECT (the named file/module/dep/service), check whether THIS
TURN's tool history contains a Read/Grep/Glob whose target matches a subject token.
  · subject read this turn  → the agent looked; trust the claim → SILENT
  · subject NOT read         → asserted blind → candidate to fire
```

**Subject extraction** (cheap, per claim class):
- *manifest*: the package token before "is a … dep" (e.g. `zod`). Subject read =
  a Read/Grep of `package.json` / `Cargo.toml` / `go.mod` / lockfile **this turn**,
  OR a Bash `cat`/`rg`/`jq` over a manifest file.
- *call-chain / authority*: the backticked or path-like noun in the sentence
  (`ingest-queue`, `rerun_tasks_for_job`, a route). Subject read = a Read/Grep/Glob
  whose `file_path`/`pattern`/`command` contains that token this turn.
- *external-mechanism*: the service is external (GitHub, fzf) — there is *no local
  file* to read, so the read-gate cannot clear it. For this class only, the carve
  that clears it is a web/lookup signal (E3's `confirmed`/`verified`, or a
  `WebSearch`/`WebFetch`/`curl` tool call this turn). If none → it fires (this is
  correct: 5/21 GitHub-ansi was asserted with neither a read nor a lookup).

```bash
# Pull this turn's read/search targets (Read/Grep/Glob inputs + cat/rg/jq Bash).
read_targets=$(printf '%s\n' "$turn_json" \
  | jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]?
      | select(.type=="tool_use")
      | if   .name=="Read"  then (.input.file_path // empty)
        elif .name=="Grep"  then (.input.pattern // "") + " " + (.input.path // "")
        elif .name=="Glob"  then (.input.pattern // "")
        elif .name=="Bash" and ((.input.command//"")|test("\\b(cat|rg|grep|jq|head|less|fd|find)\\b"))
                            then (.input.command // "")
        else empty end' 2>/dev/null)

# subject_token = the dominant noun extracted from the matched claim sentence.
# Fire only if the subject token does NOT appear in read_targets this turn.
if [ -n "$subject_token" ] && printf '%s' "$read_targets" | rg -qiF "$subject_token"; then
  exit 0   # read the subject this turn → silent
fi
```

A fire is therefore: **a checkable claim about existing code/dep/external-system,
with no in-message evidence, in a turn that never read the named subject.** That
is the exact, non-fragile signal — the conjunction the corpus shows is empty of
false positives, because in all 48 FPs at least one of (evidence-in-message,
read-this-turn) was present.

> **Why the read-gate is computed over the WHOLE turn, not the final message.**
> The claim lives in the last assistant text block (Stop-time, see §2). But the
> *read* that grounds it can be any tool call earlier in the same turn. So Stage ①
> reads the final block; Stage ③ walks the full turn's tool_use history. This is
> the act-time/stop-time split the analysis names, resolved by reading both.

---

## 2. PLACEMENT — Stop hook, with a turn-history read-gate (not PreToolUse)

**Decision: keep it a `Stop` hook** (current placement), but expand what it reads
from "final message only" to "final message + this turn's tool history."

The analysis names the act-time-vs-stop-time tradeoff precisely: *"A Stop hook is
the right place to catch a **claim**, the wrong place to catch an **action** taken
on it."* For *this* pattern, the failure **is the claim** — the agent states how a
subsystem works in prose. There is no tool call to intercept; "asserting X is the
authority" is not a Bash/Edit a PreToolUse hook could see. The damage is the false
belief entering the record (a report, a proposal, the user's plan).

| placement | what it can see | fit for *this* pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **PreToolUse** | a tool call's input, before it runs | **poor** — the claim is prose, not a tool call. PreToolUse never sees "X is the source of truth" because no tool carries it. (It is right for the *action-taken-on-a-claim* siblings — e.g. an Edit that broadens a filter on an unverified call-chain — but that's a different, action-shaped gate.) |
| **PostToolUse** | a tool's result, after it runs | poor — same reason; prose claims aren't tool results. |
| **Stop** | the completed turn: final prose **and** every tool_use/tool_result in it | **best** — the only place that sees the assertion in prose AND can check whether the subject was read this turn. The read-gate (Stage ③) is exactly the act-time signal, recovered *at* Stop by walking the turn's tool history. |
| UserPromptSubmit | next user prompt | irrelevant — too late, wrong actor. |

So the right answer is not "move it to act-time"; it is **keep it at Stop and give
it act-time vision** by reading the turn's tool calls. Stop is also where the
agent can still act on the nudge before ending — a PreToolUse fire would interrupt
mid-thought with no claim to point at.

The hook reads the **current turn** (from the last `user` message of type
non-tool-result back to the end) rather than the last 400 lines blindly, so the
read-gate is scoped to *this* turn's reads, not a stale read 5 turns ago. Concretely:
slice the tail at the last real user turn boundary.

---

## 3. RESPONSE — nudge by default, one-time stakes-scaled block only at the corner

The current hook **blocks** in high-stakes repos. A block on a 98%-FP detector is
the direct cause of mute pressure: the first false block teaches the agent the
hook is wrong, and the cheapest fix is `touch ~/.claude/.no-structural-claim-gate`.

The redesign makes the detector ~0 FP first (§1), which *earns back* the right to
some friction — but the response still defaults to the lowest-pressure form:

| condition | response | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| shape ∧ no-evidence ∧ no-read, **low-stakes** | `systemMessage` **nudge** (non-blocking) | a precise nudge rarely gets muted; the agent reads it and self-corrects or proceeds. |
| shape ∧ no-evidence ∧ no-read, **high-stakes**, **first time this claim** | one-time `decision:block` with a DO-CONFIRM | only at the corner where a wrong structural claim actually ships cost (Versable, gcc). Even here it blocks **once per claim-signature** then steps aside to a note — a residual FP costs at most one extra turn, never a trap. |
| same claim-signature already actioned | `systemMessage` note, then silent | loop-safe; never re-blocks the same sentence. |

The block reason is **specific to the matched class** — it names the subject and
says "you didn't read `<subject>` this turn," which is falsifiable and actionable,
unlike the current generic "you cite no file:line." A nudge the agent can verify
against ("I *did* read it — false positive") is a nudge it dismisses in one line
rather than mutes.

**Why not block in low-stakes too:** the empirical lesson is unambiguous — false
*blocks* drive mutes, false *nudges* mostly don't. Defaulting to nudge keeps mute
pressure at the floor; the high-stakes one-time block is the only place the
expected cost of a missed structural claim (a shipped wrong belief in production
code) justifies the friction, and even there the step-aside caps the downside.

---

## 4. FP MITIGATIONS — the exact carve-outs

Each is grounded in a specific corpus FP class (counts from the n=48 hand-read):

| # | carve-out | clears | corpus class (count) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **Drop the `owns/mints the` branch** from the regex entirely | 34/48 fires | homograph noise (71% of all fires, 0 TP) |
| M2 | **`file:line` cite** (E1, kept) | grounded claims | existing carve, retained |
| M3 | **`[UNVERIFIED]`/`[UNCONFIRMED]` hedge tag** (E1, kept) | honestly-hedged | the agent flagged its own uncertainty |
| M4 | **backtick-path cite** `` `dir/file.ts` `` (E2) | path-grounded | records 33,35,44 — agent cites by path not :line |
| M5 | **verify-verb + runtime read** (E3): confirmed/verified/ran-it/tests-pass/PID/launchctl | empirically-grounded | records 02,11,18,20,25,33,35,39,45,46 (11/48) |
| M6 | **authoring/prescription frame** (E4): ownership table row, `──►` arrow, "should/will own", "state-ownership map" | design prescriptions | records 19,24,38,40,41,47 (17/48) |
| M7 | **person/team homograph** (E5): "whoever owns", "owned by <Name>" | human-responsibility "owns" | record 32 (6/48) |
| M8 | **read-this-turn of the subject** (Stage ③): Read/Grep/Glob/cat/rg of a file matching the subject token | the agent looked | the act-time signal; the single strongest separator |
| M9 | **external-mechanism web/lookup signal**: WebSearch/WebFetch/curl this turn, or E3 verify-verb | looked-up external behavior | record 11 (fzf version-checked) |
| M10 | **meta-discussion guard**: claim text contains a quoted-pattern marker (`structural-claim`, `AUTHORITY_RX`, "the atone pattern", "this gate/hook") | discussing the rule itself | records 08,13 (4/48) — the hook firing on a discussion of the hook |
| M11 | **docs-only turn**: if this turn edited only `.md`/`.txt` and made no code edit, demote any fire to silent unless high-stakes | design-doc prose | most authoring lives in docs; pairs with M6 |
| M12 | **loop-safe signature** (kept): one action per claim-hash, then step aside | re-fires on the same sentence | existing, retained |

Carve-out evaluation order is **cheapest-first and OR-short-circuit**: E1→E2 (regex
on text, instant) → E4/E5/E10 (regex on text) → E3 (regex) → ③ read-gate (needs jq
over turn tool_use, most expensive). Any hit → silent.

**Test corpus (regression):** the 9 real S3 events in
`events-structural-claim-without-reading-code.md` are the recall set; the 48
would-fire records in `empirical-structural-claim.md` are the precision set. The
redesign must (a) keep firing on the genuine blind-assertion shapes — 5/15
call-chain, 5/21 daemon-consumes, 5/21 GitHub-ansi, 6/18 zod-manifest, all of
which were asserted with no read and no evidence — and (b) drop all 48 corpus FPs.
Build a `replay-v2.py` that ports stages ①②③ and run it over the same 959
transcripts; ship only if precision-set fires ≤ 2 AND each of the 9 recall events
(replayed with its real turn's tool history) still fires.

---

## 5. MUTE_RISK — honest assessment: **LOW**

| factor | current hook | redesign |
|---|---|---|
| corpus FP rate | ~98-100% (48/48) | projected ~0-2 fires total (selection gate) |
| default response | block (high-stakes) | nudge; block only at high-stakes ∧ blind corner |
| first-fire experience | almost certainly a false block → mute | almost certainly silent; if it fires, it names an unread subject (falsifiable) |
| dismissal cost on FP | mute the hook | one line ("I read it / verified out-of-band"), step-aside |

**Low, with two honest caveats:**

1. **Recall is structurally bounded** — the empirical doc is blunt that even a
   broadened *prose* regex reaches maybe ~4-5 of the 9 shapes; the scope-creep
